newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interim legislature pays tribute to late Deng.
newsitem.headline: HK interim legislature pays tribute to late Deng.

text.p: A shadow legislature to be installed when Beijing takes over Hong Kong began a meeting in southern China on Saturday with three minutes of silent tribute to Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping.

At the start of the meeting, held across the border in the city of Shenzhen, Provisional Legislature president Rita Fan praised Deng, who died on Wednesday, for his concept of "one country, two systems", Hong Kong's Cable TV reported.

The "one country, two systems" principle for Hong Kong's return to China at midnight on June 30 allows the territory to retain considerable autonomy and keep its capitalist way of life for 50 years after the sovereignty transfer.
The meeting was the second since the 60-member interim body was chosen by a 400-strong Beijing-anointed caucus in December.
The controversial assembly will replace Hong Kong's elected legislature, reversing Colonial Governor Chris Patten's democratic reforms in the dying days of British rule.

"Mr Deng Xiaoping believed Hong Kong people can run Hong Kong and believed international disputes (on Hong Kong's return to China) can be resolved through 'one country, two systems'," Fan told the interim assembly.
She vowed that the provisional legislature would carry out its duty to ensure a smooth transition to Chinese rule.
Britain and the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong have condemned the establishment of the provisional assembly, saying it was unnecessary and illegal.
The Democratic Party, the territory's largest, has threatened a legal challenge to the interim body on the grounds it is constitutionally illegal to have two legislatures operating at the same time.
This has prompted the provisional legislature to hold its meetings in Shenzhen.
Saturday's meeting agreed to set up two panels to work out administrative and procedural arrangements for the interim body, Cable TV said.
The interim chamber decided to call another meeting in a month's time, the television station reported.

Members hoped that at the next meeting they would have all necessary rules and secretarial support in place to start dealing with bills to be presented by the administration of the territory's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, local radio said.

Tasks to be handled by the interim body before the handover include preparing laws to define permanent residency status and the territory's post-handover flag, and possibly laws on freedom of assembly.
It will also approve the transitional budget and the appointment of top judges.
